problems.basis: BE/AI reviewed (#16 R1). Every code in the Problem.code enum, one fixture per code holding that code's DEFAULT face. apps/api ProblemFixtureContractTest now pins type/title/status/retryable to io.nullnull.shared.problem.ProblemCode, so these four can no longer drift from what the server answers with; the review found APPLY_FAILED carrying retryable true, which contradicted both the enum and docs/api/README.md's statement that only ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and RATE_LIMITED are retryable. requestId is a UUIDv7 because that is what RequestIdFilter generates (the earlier ULID was a shape the server never produces on its own). NOT verified here: `detail` is the contract's English fallback and is deliberately generic rather than the literal sentence a given throw site uses (README says the raising slice owns that sentence, and FE renders its own copy from `code`); `instance` is a plausible path, not a captured one, except for DELETION_STATUS_EXPIRED which has exactly one throw site. NOT COVERED: the codes README's UI mapping table gives a second status - INVALID_REQUEST 400/405/406/413/415, LOCK_CONFLICT 409/422, APPLY_FAILED 500/503 - have no variant fixture, because the index is keyed by code and holds one entry per code. 9 of the 23 codes have no throw site in apps/api yet (it was 11 before BA-030~034 landed).

session.basis: Bootstrap trio needed to exercise the 401 retry and CSRF reissue policies. deletion-receipt.statusUrl now carries the /api/v1 server base, matching what DeletionService actually emits; it previously omitted it and the contract constrained neither, so both spellings passed. The contract now describes statusUrl as an API path and DeletionIT pins its prefix to spring.mvc.servlet.path so the literal and the configured path cannot drift. BE/AI reviewed (#16 R1): DeletionStatus is a plain record with no @JsonInclude, so the server really does send completedAt, failureCode and retryable rather than omitting them, and the fixture's retryable false with status RUNNING matches the rule that retryable is true exactly while status is PARTIAL_FAILED. Three more DeletionRequestStatus fixtures cover COMPLETED, PARTIAL_FAILED and FAILED: every field is decided by apps/api (JdbcDeletionStore.markCompleted clears failureCode and sets completedAt; markFailed sets completedAt only when the status is FAILED), so FAILED carries a completedAt while PARTIAL_FAILED does not - which is exactly why terminality is read from status and never from completedAt. These are derived from the server's own write paths rather than invented, but no captured response backs them, so serverVerified stays false. owner-profile-onboarded.json (#16) is updatePreferences' response example, pinned by check-examples.mjs: the anonymous owner after onboarding with trip-detail-scheduled's trip active. OwnerPreferencesIT compares its keys with a real response and validates that response against OwnerProfile.

trips.basis: BE/AI authored. candidates is empty while candidateCount is 5 on purpose: the contract states that candidates is a bounded view and listTripCandidates is the paginated source, so the array length is never the total. trip-detail-interests is its own trip with its own trip-page entry, not a second face of trip-detail-scheduled. They previously shared one id AND version 3 while holding different day items, which made the ETag - a quoted trip version - claim one validator for two materially different bodies. Each detail fixture now maps to exactly one row in trip-page.json, and the openapi.yaml response examples are generated from these files and pinned to them by packages/contracts/scripts/check-examples.mjs. The places inside day items now use the HS/11 pair like the places set: categoryCode and regionCode are opaque and provider-derived per the contract, so an invented taxonomy such as ATTRACTION/KR-11-110 does not satisfy it. Only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call; the others share its SHAPE and are not themselves verified provider values. Wall-clock times lost their +09:00 offset (#145): the contract declared startTime and suggestedTime as format: time, which is RFC 3339 full-time and REQUIRES an offset, while ERD.md stores them in a PostgreSQL `time` column that cannot hold one and README.md calls them offset-less local time. The contract was the outlier, and it let "09:30:00Z" through - which the column would have silently reduced to 09:30 local, nine hours off for a Seoul trip. The fields now carry an explicit HH:mm:ss pattern and these values match it. trip-detail-reservation.json is new (#144): no fixture anywhere carried a RESERVATION lock while four Frontend code paths branch on one. It is its OWN trip with its own trip-page row rather than a lock added to trip-detail-scheduled, because that fixture's unlocked third item is the thing FE-307 uses to exercise 'a lock can still be set here' - adding one would have removed the case rather than added one. draft-preview-ready.json and draft-preview-empty.json (BA-055, previewTripDraft) are the two response examples of that operation: the places are copied from places/search-page.json so one id renders one summary everywhere, and the stop layout follows the apps/ai composer's rule (place id ascending, fewest stops first, earliest date on a tie) so the example does not show an answer the service could not give. Schema-shaped, not captured from a server. The seven mutation-*.json files (#16) are the response examples of addTripItem, updateTripItem, reorderTripItems, replaceTripItem, setTripItemConstraint, removeTripItemConstraint and removeTripItem, pinned by check-examples.mjs. Their SHAPE is the server's: TripMutationFixtureIT builds trip-detail-scheduled's trip over HTTP (the same places, locks, candidate-backed 명동 and five candidates), makes each change, and compares every level's keys; each captured response validated against TripMutationResult before the file was written. Their VALUES are the captured ones with trip-detail-scheduled's ids mapped in by place (the IT asserts which item each changedItemIds names, which is what the mapping rests on), its ACTIVE status, and version 4. So they follow the server's order (interests by code, each item's locks by type - JdbcTripStore's ORDER BY) and carry no items[].crowd. #16 item 3b brought trip-detail-scheduled and trip-detail-reservation to the same place keys (categoryName and regionName null, as the server sends them) and the same order, and trip-detail-interests to the same interest order; TripMutationFixtureIT compares getTrip with the first two, keys and order. The places carry the KTO credit in sourceAttribution: TripMutationFixtureIT references each place to KTO_KOR_SERVICE_2 revision 4 the way the canonical ingest does, so the server sends the credit on getTrip and on every mutation, and the values are the ones places/search-page.json carries for the same 경복궁 id. They were null before only because the test places had no external reference; the server sends null for a place with no external source. BA-030-T5 checks the credit's values against the source registry revision and BA-030-T6 the null, and both fixture ITs assert that every place in a response they compare is credited, because the key-set comparison merges array elements and cannot see one place losing it. They still hold items[].crowd: null, a key the server does not send: that waits for #105, because an FE test reads the fixture's null, and the comparison takes the path out by name only while the fixture holds it.

optimizations.basis: NO approved example exists for listOptimizationHistory. Values invented to match Figma S14 422:2925 (applied/kept/reverted, and an empty variant) and validated against the schema only. Replace with BE/AI's real response (BA-053). run-ready.json and run-applied.json (getOptimization, #16 R3) are BE/AI authored and are the operation's two response examples, pinned by check-examples.mjs. Their SHAPE is the server's: OptimizeItemIT and OptimizeRevertIT compare the keys at every level with a real response, and a captured response validated against OptimizationRun before these were written. Their VALUES follow the production formats (KtoForecastResponseValidator's kto-tats- issue ids, JdbcKtoForecastSnapshotStore's scope label, the V007/V011 registry text, the apps/ai KO explanation template, whose particles follow the preceding sound since #260) and continue the other fixtures: run-applied is history-page's APPLIED ITEM run, and its APPLY moved 명동 onto 10-05, producing trip-detail-scheduled's version 3; run-ready is a later preview on that version for 인사동, whose TIME lock is why its one check is listed. Every proposal is comparison-eligible because ProposalRevalidator refuses an ineligible candidate (VERDICT_INELIGIBLE), so no ineligible proposal is ever stored. run-queued, run-failed and the three decision-* files (#16) are the rest of the flow and are pinned the same way: run-queued is createOptimization's 202 example, run-failed getOptimization's FAILED example, decision-apply and decision-keep decideOptimization's, decision-revert revertOptimizationDecision's. Each shape was taken from a captured response that validated against its schema, and OptimizeItemIT / OptimizeRevertIT compare every level's keys with the server's. Their values continue the same story: run-queued is run-ready's run at the moment it was queued; run-failed a later ITEM run on the same version that found no forecast (DATA_INSUFFICIENT, the server's message); decision-apply is the APPLY run-applied lists; decision-keep is history-page's KEPT run; decision-revert undoes decision-apply at 06:30, after run-ready's preview expired and inside revertUntil, producing version 4. Not captured values, so serverVerified stays false for the set.

crowd.basis: BE/AI authored (#16). getPlaceCrowdForecast's three faces - series-forecast (FORECAST), series-stale (the same forecast served as a STALE fallback) and series-unavailable (NO_COVERAGE) - are the operation's response examples, pinned by check-examples.mjs. Their SHAPE is the server's: each was taken from a captured response that validated against CrowdSeries, and CrowdForecastApiIT compares every level's keys with a real response. Their VALUES continue the optimization fixtures: all three are 명동, the place run-applied moved; series-forecast's three points are the snapshots its proposals compared (same set, issue and provenanceId) with the values their summaries quote (34, 72.5, 51); series-stale is the 10-06 point read after the set's staleAt with no newer set, so the server's fallback fields (state and sourceState STALE, fallbackUsed true, comparisonEligible false with STALE_INPUT) and its label for a stale point are set. The labels are CrowdProvenanceProjection's. forecast-query.json (#105) is queryPlaceCrowdForecasts' response example, pinned the same way: four cards in request order - 명동 fresh (series-forecast's three points unchanged, answering an id that was merged into 명동, so its placeId is 명동's rather than the id sent), 경복궁 as a STALE fallback from its own older set, 북촌한옥마을 with no stored forecast (NO_COVERAGE), and an id no place has (PLACE_UNAVAILABLE, placeId equal to the id sent). 경복궁's point, its set, run and issue ids are authored in the production formats, not taken from a call. Its SHAPE is the server's: CrowdForecastQueryIT compares every level's keys with a real batch response. Not captured values, so serverVerified stays false for the set. forecast-query-request.json is the request forecast-query.json answers (#105): Frontend asked for it because a mock that pairs a response with its request by id cannot know that the first id was merged into 명동, and answers it PLACE_UNAVAILABLE. placeIds[0] (...2b06) is authored for the example and used nowhere else in the repository; what the server does with a merged id - the item keeps the request position and names the canonical place - is BA-023-T7 in CrowdForecastQueryIT. The other three ids are the response items' own, in the same order, and from/to are the window the response example describes. It is the first request example in the contract, so check-examples.mjs now reads requestBody examples too and pins this one to the file.

candidates.basis: NO approved example exists for listTripCandidates, getCandidateTripMatches or addTripItem. Values invented to match Figma S07-8 412:1912 (an active candidate, a SIMILAR one, one already SCHEDULED, one with no external source, an empty variant) plus one match result per state so EXACT/SIMILAR/NONE/CHECKING/UNKNOWN are each exercised rather than collapsed. Three places carry the KTO credit PlaceSummary.sourceAttribution holds and one carries null; those values are authored, not compared with a server response - CandidateIT compares a place's keys at one level only. The null one is a place with NO external source at all (...2b05), not a credited place stripped of its credit: JdbcCatalogPlaceQuery returns null for sourceAttribution exactly when the place_external_refs lateral is empty, and the contract says "Null only for records with no external source". 명동 (...2b02) held that role until #287 and was the corpus's only self-contradicting id - reading the sourceAttribution beside that id in every fixture of this repository gave 13 credited and this one null - so it is credited here too now and that reading gives 14 credited, 0 null. The unattributed place is ACTIVE, so the role sits on a candidate card rather than a scheduled row, which is what CMP-ATT-003 measures; its name is the one TripMutationFixtureIT uses, 외부 출처가 없는 장소, the shape BA-030-T6 proves the server answers with no credit. Frontend approved the move and that exact name on #287. The items run in ASCENDING createdAt while JdbcCandidateStore.page answers created_at DESC, id ASC: a deviation this file carried before #287 and that #287 did not touch, because items[0] and items[2] are position-bound by Frontend tests. The new item was appended with the latest timestamp so the array follows one rule rather than none; putting the page in the server's order is its own change and needs those bindings moved first. Replace with BE/AI's real response (BA-034, BA-042). Place codes use the HS/11 pair: categoryCode and regionCode are opaque and provider-derived per the contract, so an invented taxonomy does not satisfy it. Only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call - the others share its SHAPE and are not themselves verified provider values. categoryName and regionName are null because JdbcCatalogPlaceQuery returns null for both until a reviewed code-to-label mapping exists; a fixture that fills them promises a label the server cannot produce. save-result-created.json and save-result-duplicate.json are new: addTripCandidate had no CandidateSaveResult fixture anywhere, so FE's msw handler was the de-facto contract for it. Both carry tripScheduleChanged false, which is invariant 2 in the response shape rather than in prose. Wall-clock times lost their +09:00 offset (#145): the contract declared startTime and suggestedTime as format: time, which is RFC 3339 full-time and REQUIRES an offset, while ERD.md stores them in a PostgreSQL `time` column that cannot hold one and README.md calls them offset-less local time. The contract was the outlier, and it let "09:30:00Z" through - which the column would have silently reduced to 09:30 local, nine hours off for a Seoul trip. The fields now carry an explicit HH:mm:ss pattern and these values match it. BA-034 landed, and CandidateIT now compares save-result-created.json and save-result-duplicate.json against REAL server responses - which keys exist at each level, the status, the nullness of scheduledTripItemId, and the two fields that carry the operation's meaning (duplicate, tripScheduleChanged). They matched without being changed to match; the comparison is of shape rather than values because ids, timestamps and place names differ by construction. The other seven files in this set are still un-compared: getCandidateTripMatches is BA-042 and candidate-page is not yet read back this way, so serverVerified stays false for the set as a whole.

feed.basis: listFeed has no OpenAPI example. Built to cover every state S03-F0 `391:310` and S03-F1 `396:2926` have to render: all four candidateState values, a FORECAST crowd reading and an UNAVAILABLE one, a post with no excerpt, and a second page so pagination is walked rather than assumed. Crowd provenance is copied from the related-places fixture rather than retyped, because DataProvenance requires 29 fields. Page size is 4, not the contract default of 20. Place codes use the HS/11 pair: categoryCode and regionCode are opaque and provider-derived per the contract, so an invented taxonomy does not satisfy it. Only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call - the others share its SHAPE and are not themselves verified provider values. categoryName and regionName are null because JdbcCatalogPlaceQuery returns null for both until a reviewed code-to-label mapping exists; a fixture that fills them promises a label the server cannot produce. Split into two pages (#156): a single page could never carry NO_TRIP_SELECTED beside the other states, because that value describes the REQUEST - no tripId was supplied - and so applies to every card or none. page.json is now the tripId-supplied page and page-no-trip.json the one without, which is also what FeedScreen needs: it branches to S03-F0 or S03-F1 on whether a trip is selected, and one file could not draw the first. The contract now states that semantics on candidateState rather than leaving it to be inferred. page-2.json now carries a second card whose crowd reading is STALE (#FE-201-T2). It was added rather than converted from an existing one because the suite's other cases derive their expectations from these items, and it went in page-2.json rather than page.json because check-examples.mjs pins FIXTURE_OF.feedPage to page.json byte for byte - editing that file forces an identical edit to the feedPage example in docs/api/openapi.yaml, which is a contract change, while page-2.json is pinned to no example and is still ajv-validated through feedFixtures.pageTwo. Its provenance is the FORECAST card's, changed only where staleness actually shows, so nothing about the reading is invented (invariant 8): sourceState and freshness STALE; fetchedAt 2026-09-04 with staleAt 2026-09-05, a week older than the fresh cards and expired six days before they were fetched, so 'old' is readable from the fixture instead of asserted; forecastIssueId 2026-09-04, an older issue than the fresh cards' 2026-09-11, which is WHY it is not comparable; confidence null and comparisonEligible false with comparisonReasonCode STALE_INPUT, the same pairing crowd/series-stale.json uses, because a stale reading does not carry its old confidence forward and may not be compared numerically; fallbackUsed true because the last value is what is being shown. value 58 is synthetic in the same way every number in this set is - it keeps the fresh card's unit and diagnostic label and differs only in age - and the feed card does not render it at all (CrowdLevel draws ordinalLevel, which is null here as on every other card). observedAtSkewSeconds stays 0 to match this file's other crowd cards rather than series-stale.json's null; both validate.

system.basis: BE/AI authored from the operations controllers. Mixed evidence, stated per file rather than collapsed into one flag. demo-readiness-not-ready.json is PROVEN: apps/api's DemoReadinessContractTest builds the real DemoCapabilityQuery with every flag OFF and asserts it produces exactly that document, so its detail strings are the server's own. NOT_READY with three UNAVAILABLE capabilities is the correct P0 answer - every flag ships OFF. The detail strings say WHICH of the two reasons each one is unavailable for, and they no longer say the same thing: optimization (BA-050) and live (B10) now have a server-side source and are off by decision, while replay still has none and a FEATURE_REPLAY_MODE turned ON fails startup rather than advertising it; there is no READY or DEGRADED fixture because producing one would be a claim about behaviour that does not exist. health-live.json and readiness-ready.json are DERIVED, not proven: the values come from HealthController (status UP; checks named database, jobs and recommendation with detail null, because every probe returns null detail when READY) but no test regenerates them, so a probe renaming itself would not be caught here. NOT_READY is absent from readiness-ready.json on purpose - HealthController throws 503 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE instead of answering 200 in that state. serverVerified stays false for the set because two of the three are not captured or proven.

imports.basis: BE/AI authored (#16). draft-needs-review, draft-ready and confirmed-trip are the response examples of parseTripImport, remapTripImport and confirmTripImport, pinned by check-examples.mjs. Their places carry the KTO credit: TripImportFixtureIT references each seeded place to KTO_KOR_SERVICE_2 revision 4 the way the canonical ingest does, so the server credits them as it does on getTrip, and the fixtures match the trip set for the same ids. Their SHAPE is the server's: TripImportFixtureIT runs a synthetic paste (three places that resolve, one line that matches two) through parse, remap and confirm over HTTP and compares every level's keys, and each captured response validated against its schema before the file was written. Their VALUES are the captured ones with the places mapped to the other sets' ids by name (서울숲 공원 is the one new place), new draft, trip and item ids, and an expiresAt 24 hours after a parse at 2026-09-30T09:00:00Z. live.basis: BA-091 Backend/AI 계약 제안. queryLiveAreas, listLiveAreaPlaces, getLivePlace의 요청·응답 예시 11건을 OpenAPI에 넣고 check-examples.mjs로 fixture와 정확히 고정했다. 서울 값은 숫자가 아닌 검토된 1~4 단계(A-060)이며 value/unit은 null이다. sourceRegistryVersion=2, normalizationVersion=seoul-live-area-v1, scopeLabel과 attribution은 V046 및 서버 projection을 따른다. LiveAreaReadIT와 LivePlaceApiIT가 실제 HTTP 응답의 단계·label·출처·mapping·comparisonReasonCode 등 핵심 필드를 대조했다. 지역 관측은 DIRECT, 장소에 표시한 값은 AREA/AREA_FALLBACK이고, 관측 없는 매핑의 crowd는 null·mappingType은 NONE이다. 이 예시의 날짜·UUID·장소 데이터는 합성이며 실제 서울 API capture나 전체 응답 일치 증거가 아니므로 serverVerified=false다. 11건은 packages/contracts/src/index.ts로 export하고 apps/web fixtures.test.ts에서 모든 응답과 LivePlace 배열을 검사한다. FE 승인은 미완료이며 화면 의미와 persistent badge 구현은 FE 검토가 필요하다. 서울의 단계는 각 지역의 과거 평균에 상대적이므로 지역 간 혼잡 비교에 사용하지 않는다. 위치 좌표와 지역 경계는 공급자가 제공하지 않아 null이다.
